headline: 481 people killed in August road accidents, RSF report
summary: Road crash deaths rose by about 65 compared to July, with motorcyclists accounting for the largest share of fatalities.
details: A total of 513 road crashes were recorded in August, leaving 481 people dead and 664 injured, according to the Road Safety Foundation (RSF).

caption:
481 lives lost in a single month. Road crash deaths in Bangladesh rose in August, with motorcyclists facing the highest risk.

A total of 513 road crashes were recorded in August, leaving 481 people dead and 664 injured, according to the Road Safety Foundation (RSF).

Motorcyclists were the most affected, with 176 deaths in 183 crashes, accounting for 36.59% of all fatalities.

Pedestrians accounted for 102 deaths (21.20%), while 67 drivers and their assistants also lost their lives.

The victims included 61 students, 58 children, and 61 women, among various other professional groups.

Loss of vehicle control was the leading cause of crashes with 195 incidents, followed by head-on collisions and pedestrians being hit.

Dhaka division recorded the highest number of crashes (172) and deaths (144), while Bogura district had the highest death toll with 37 fatalities.

The RSF identified excessive speed, reckless driving, faulty vehicles, and poor road design as major causes of these accidents.

The foundation recommended technology-based speed monitoring, better driver training, and reforms to road safety institutions.

headline_marked: Gazipur court [[rejects bail for Sifat]] in anti-terrorism case
headline: Gazipur court rejects bail for Sifat in anti-terrorism case
summary: Sifat Abdullah was arrested for alleged derogatory remarks against the prime minister and is now facing charges under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
details: A Gazipur court has rejected the bail petition of Sifat Abdullah, who was arrested following alleged derogatory remarks against the prime minister. The order was passed by Gazipur Metropolitan Magistrate Court-5 Judge Rakibul Islam.

Sifat's lawyers argued that the alleged abusive language regarding the electricity and energy crisis was not mentioned in the first information report (FIR). They further claimed that Sifat had no connection to the case filed on June 4 and is facing political harassment.

Sifat is an active member of the National Citizen Party (NCP) and was previously involved in the 'anti-fascist movement' and Inqilab Mancha. Ali Naser, central joint chief organiser of the NCP, described the arrest as a new form of fascism.

Police sources state that Sifat was detained from his residence in Gazipur by Gacha Police Station officers on September 3. He was later shown arrested in the old case and sent to jail on September 4.
